newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Tranz Rail to invest $75 mln this year.
newsitem.headline: Tranz Rail to invest $75 mln this year.

text.p: New Zealand rail and ferry operator Tranz Rail said on Tuesday it would invest NZ$75 million this year on infrastructure and spend more than NZ$600 million over 10 years to modify and replace its ships and terminals.

He said key objectives were: to improve customer service even further; expand the revenue base from emerging and existing traffics; upgrade the asset base; cut costs and lift productivity; offer incentives to employees; and improve operational practices to ensure the health and safety of staff.
It expected to benefit from strong growth in the forestry sector, with rail lines adjacent to many forests and new rolling stock to carry forestry products.
Tranz Rail should also benefit from increased export production by state-owned Coal Corporation, to 3.0 million tonnes in 2000 from 1.4 million in 1996.
There was interest from other commodity groups in the use of rail to carry milk, concrete and roading aggregates, refuse (from urban centres to rural landfills) and petroleum.
Tranz Rail's majority shareholder is Wisconsin Central Transportation Corp..
